clue.text: Punishment with nine-inch ruler

parts.note: a span is the old measure of a hand's stretch, nine inches
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A teacher punishes a pupil with a ruler nine inches long.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ruler' looks like the instrument of punishment, but it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking given as a penalty, especially to a child, is this sort of chastisement.

clue.text: Gives away secret of acrobatic feat

definitions.meaning: informs or tells tales, as in split on someone
a gymnast's move with the legs stretched out flat in opposite directions

explanation.surface: A gymnast reveals the secret of a stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to split on someone is to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for informing, and also the gymnast's move with both legs flat on the floor.

clue.text: A nurse takes time to be there

indicators.note: takes means the first part admits the abbreviation for time into it

parts.note: to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse makes time to be present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' puts T inside A TEND, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event or meeting.

clue.text: Country's livelihood, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a career is one's livelihood

explanation.surface: A nation's livelihood, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent CAREER and the Asian country sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the East Asian peninsula, divided into North and South.

clue.text: Wagon caught in dread rain, yet it's heavenly!

definitions.note: a clause defining a noun: the state of bliss is what is heavenly

indicators.note: caught in means the vehicle sits inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A wagon trapped in dreadful rain, yet somehow it feels like paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dread' rearranges RAIN as NIRA; 'caught in' puts VAN inside it after NIR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the final state of bliss and release is a kind of paradise.

clue.text: Leftwing writer unhappy with Blair?

parts.note: the socialist author of Animal Farm was born Eric Blair, so a writer who disliked that name chose a pen name; the surface suggests a critic of Tony Blair

explanation.surface: A left-wing columnist is disappointed with Prime Minister Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the Labour Prime Minister when this appeared; the Blair meant is the writer's own birth surname, which he set aside for a pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Nineteen Eighty-Four, a socialist, published under a pseudonym instead of his real surname Blair.

clue.text: Strange insects go around in cattle

indicators.note: go around means the two words surround the little word that follows

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange
ants are insects

explanation.surface: Odd insects are crawling about among the cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is British slang for odd. RUM and ANTS 'go around' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud-chewing animals such as cows, sheep and goats; cattle are the prime example.

clue.text: Start off exclusion could mean the sack

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: rejection is exclusion

explanation.surface: Being left out from the start could mean losing your job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' drops the first letter, R, of REJECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown out or dismissed from a job is getting the sack.

definitions.note: an adjective phrase defining a noun: the tiny single-celled creature is the thing that is very, very small

clue.text: Obscure leaders in be located under ruins

parts.note: Ur is a ruined ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Leaders find their plans obscured beneath the ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city, survives only as ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something indistinct or hard to see is to make it fuzzy.

clue.text: Valiant sort gets two ducks, quite useless

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a duck is a nought in cricket, so two of them are two letter Os

explanation.surface: A brave fellow is out for nought twice, which is no use to his team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, written O. 'sort' rearranges VALIANT together with OO.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an effort that achieves nothing, so wholly ineffective.

clue.text: No signs of old city in natural region of Africa

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city of the Chaldees

explanation.surface: A naturalist finds no trace of an ancient city in an African landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No signs of' removes UR, the biblical city, from NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A former province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal, so a part of the continent.

clue.text: Sensible patients wouldn't be in one

definitions.text: Sensible patients wouldn't be in one

parts.words: Sensible patients wouldn't be in one

explanation.surface: Patients with good sense would never get themselves into some predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' suggests good judgement; its older sense is 'aware, conscious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of prolonged unconsciousness, which no conscious patient can be in.

clue.text: Tubs are OK to con explosions

indicators.note: to con is to trick, so the letters of the phrase are turned about deceptively

explanation.surface: Someone claims that the tubs are safe in order to trick people about the explosions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' asks you to rearrange TUBS ARE OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden eruptions, of violence or disease, are bursts of activity.

clue.text: River in swollen condition -sound the alarm!

parts.note: R is the standard map abbreviation for river
gout is an illness that swells the joints

explanation.surface: A river in flood prompts a warning to be raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swollen condition' reads as a river in spate, but it is the illness gout; IN is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells peal loudly, so to make that peal is to give a warning signal.

explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club; 'goal' means an aim here, not a score.

clue.text: Set free of charges yet bound over

definitions.meaning: acquit, as a court does a defendant
leap over, as a horse does a fence

explanation.surface: A court releases a defendant without charge but binds them over to keep the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound over' looks like the legal phrase for a court order; here it means jumping over something.
explanation.definitionFit: A court may acquit a suspect, and a jumper may vault an obstacle without touching it: both senses of one verb.

clue.text: Garden features fashioned from stones around lake

clue.text: I join cold march, on retreat in frozen north

clue.text: Upholder of standards
